likely_official_source_authorities_neede.financial_intelligence_unit_or_aml_autho: Unidad de Inteligencia Financiera (UIF, Secretaría de Hacienda)

candidates.expected_difficulty: Low-medium. Central bank and customs sources already on file internally; primary sources are Spanish-language and require careful translation review before citation.
known_risk_areas: Spanish-language source translation accuracy

P8G-1 finding (2026-07-25): the on-file data/rules/mexico.json control claims are UNSUPPORTED by the sources verified in P8G-1 and require claim-specific verification or removal at P8G-2 (they must not be preserved merely because they are on file). Mexico operates a market-determined FREE-FLOATING exchange regime since 22 Dec 1994, set by the Comisión de Cambios (SHCP + Banco de México) — this verifies the exchange-rate-determination MECHANISM only and does NOT by itself establish the presence or absence of any general exchange-control, approval, or capital-movement restriction. Unsupported on-file phrases: country_overview 'subject to certain capital flow management measures and reporting requirements'; summary.traveler 'Export of foreign currency is restricted and subject to Banxico rules'; take_foreign_currency_out 'up to the amount declared on entry ... Residents are subject to Banxico limits'; resident_holding_rules 'Banxico limits and approval requirements ... unrestricted access requires specific authorisation'; summary.business 'Capital repatriation and certain payments require Banxico approval or documentation'; exchange_controls 'controls on certain capital account transactions'. At P8G-2 each must be either substantiated with a claim-matched official legal/regulatory source (e.g. Ley del Banco de México / Ley Monetaria, Banxico circulars) or removed. Whether Mexican law imposes any general exchange-control/approval/capital-movement restriction is itself a P8G-2 verification target and must NOT be asserted (in either direction) without such a source — the P8G-1 result is that the old claims are unsupported, not that the opposite is established.

P8G-1 finding: the mandatory border cash declaration is set by LEY ADUANERA Article 9o (current text, última reforma DOF 19-11-2025), verbatim: any person entering or leaving national territory carrying cash, national or foreign checks, payment orders or any other collectible document, or a COMBINATION of them, EXCEEDING the equivalent of ten thousand US dollars, is obliged to declare it to the customs authorities on the official forms approved by the SAT — symmetric on entry AND exit; a second paragraph obliges users of international valuables-transport/courier services to declare shipments above the same threshold. Penalty: Ley Aduanera Art. 185 fracción VII — a fine of 20% to 40% of the amount exceeding USD 10,000. On-file cash_declaration_threshold ('USD 10,000 or equivalent') should be tightened to 'exceeding/superior to' USD 10,000 aggregating cash + national/foreign checks + payment orders + other collectible documents (or a combination), mandatory to customs, SAT-approved forms, at P8G-2.

P8G-1 finding: the operational border authority is now ANAM (Agencia Nacional de Aduanas de México), created by presidential decree DOF 14-07-2021 and operational from 2022; the Ley Aduanera Art. 9 forms remain 'approved by the SAT'. The on-file source label 'Mexican Customs (SAT)' should be updated at P8G-2 to reflect ANAM as the customs operator with SAT-approved forms.

P8G-1 finding: keep six regimes strictly separate at P8G-2 — (a) Ley Aduanera Art. 9 customs border cash declaration (>USD 10,000); (b) foreign-exchange regulation (market-determined float set by the Comisión de Cambios SHCP+Banxico; the existence of any general exchange-control/approval restriction is a P8G-2 verification target, not established here); (c) bank/intermediary reporting and the separate anti-dollarization limits banks apply to US-dollar CASH deposits (a cash-handling restriction, NOT a capital control); (d) UIF AML/CFT reporting; (e) SAT tax/information reporting; (f) LFPIORPI (Ley Antilavado) domestic cash-PAYMENT limits on certain high-value transactions. None may be conflated; in particular the bank USD-cash-deposit caps and the LFPIORPI cash-payment limits must not be presented as exchange controls or as border rules.

P8G-1 note: environment reachability (2026-07-25) — diputados.gob.mx Ley Aduanera PDF fetched HTTP 200 (Art. 9 + penalty extracted verbatim); gob.mx SHCP 'Anuncio de la Comisión de Cambios', gob.mx/hacienda/uif (UIF) and gob.mx/cnbv (CNBV) all HTTP 200; banxico.org.mx main and mercados pages HTTP 200. ANAM (anam.gob.mx) and some deep Banxico paths WAF-block the fetch/curl bot (HTTP 403/000) but content is confirmed via official search results and the diputados primary law. Exact article pinpoints for the FX-regime legal basis (Ley del Banco de México / Ley Monetaria; Comisión de Cambios), the CNBV intermediary framework, the UIF/LFPIORPI AML citations, and the bank USD-cash-deposit limits are to be pinned at P8G-2.

P8G-2 outcome (2026-07-29, first CRES application): data/rules/mexico.json CONTENT CORRECTED and CRES-classified against claim-matched primary sources — Ley Aduanera Art. 9 / Art. 185 (customs, E0), Ley del Banco de México Art. 21-22 (Comisión de Cambios statutory authority independently E0; the composite current-free-floating-regime claim graded E1, resting on SHCP/Banxico institutional confirmation, with no hybrid E0/E1 notation), Ley Monetaria Art. 8 (foreign currency not legal tender; FX obligations settled in pesos at the exchange rate, E0), Ley de Instituciones de Crédito Art. 115 (AML basis for US-dollar cash limits, E1), plus SHCP/Banxico/CNBV/UIF. Per CRES §7 the on-file over-statements ('Banxico approval', 'capital flow management measures', 'export restricted', 'Banxico limits') were removed and recorded as unsupported — NOT replaced with an unsupported 'no controls' absolute; the free-float regime and settlement framework are substantiated, while the exhaustive absence of any exchange-control/capital-movement restriction outside the statutes examined is a bounded E2 verification item. Six regimes kept separate (customs / FX regime / LIC Art. 115 bank AML cash caps / UIF AML / SAT tax / LFPIORPI cash-payment limits). page_status stays verified, indexing_allowed false, no public surface; no CRES schema fields added (structural prototype deferred). All five governance gates pass. Mexico HELD at source_review_ready (publication not sought). Review-Gate corrections before merge (2026-07-29): (1) the no-authorisation-regime claim downgraded E1 -> E2 bounded and reworded as a bounded review finding, not a legal negative; (2) resident_holding_rules and non_resident_rules converted to CRES E3 verification targets (the sources do not establish account eligibility/operation/repatriation); (3) deferred AML numeric detail (monthly caps, account-holder categories) removed from the rule data until P8G-2b; (4) the unsourced '1982 exchange-control decree superseded' statement removed; (5) the exchange-rate-regime claim recorded at claim level, with the statutory-authority sub-claim kept E0 but the composite free-floating-regime claim kept E1 rather than any mixed grade. Open items for a later P8G-2b: E3 resident/non-resident account-regime source, the E2 bounded exchange-control-absence, and the current US-dollar cash-operation thresholds/categories under LIC Art. 115.
